info.title: deepertones API
info.description: Every JSON response has an envelope, and `status` equals the HTTP status. Success: `{ success: true, status, message, data }`. Error: `{ success: false, status, message, error: { code, details?, requestId } }`. Branch on `success`, then on `error.code`, not on `message`.

status.description: `degraded` when any check is down.
The HTTP status code, repeated for clients that only keep the body.

details.description: Extra context. For VALIDATION_FAILED: a list of `{ path, message }`, one per invalid field.

requestId.description: Also sent as the X-Request-Id header. Quote it when reporting a bug.

refreshToken.description: Send only to `/api/v1/auth/refresh`. Lives 60 days from each use.

status.description: `anonymous` is a guest; `verified` has proven an email or phone.

deviceId.description: A stable id for this install: Android `getAndroidId`, or a UUID kept in the iOS Keychain.

profiles.description: Every profile of the account, the default first.

Profile.description: The profile this session is on.

deviceId.description: The same stable install id the app sends to `/api/v1/auth/anonymous`.

token.description: The Expo push token, `ExponentPushToken[...]`. Anything else is 400 `PUSH_TOKEN_INVALID`.

deviceId.description: The same stable install id the app sends to `/api/v1/auth/anonymous`.

scanFinished.description: Tell me when a scan is ready.

scanNeedsYou.description: Tell me when a scan needs a photo or a confirmation from me.

imageUrl.description: The product's stock image, an absolute URL, if it has one.

products.description: At most 10, best first: those whose search text (brand, name and variant, normalised) starts with the query, then the others, each group by that text.

items.description: One per photo, in photo order.

position.description: The photo's place in the upload, from 0.

state.description: `ready`, `rejected`, `failed` and `unidentified` are final. `needs-confirmation` waits for the corrected product, `needs-back-photo` for a photo of the ingredient list and `needs-retake` for a new photo of the front (see `retakesLeft`); `needs-identification` is where an item lands once its 3rd front photo could not be read; `unidentified` is where it ends when the user says the product has no label (see `noLabel`); the others are being worked on.

reason.description: Why the item is `rejected` or `failed`, or why it asks for the back photo again (`label-unreadable`; also the reason it fails once the 3rd back photo cannot be read), or why its front photo could not be used (`unreadable`, or `label-not-visible` when a product is in view but its label is turned away or covered), in `needs-retake` and `needs-identification`.

retakesLeft.description: Only on an item in `needs-retake`: how many more front photos it may be sent. Absent in every other state.

recognised.description: What the photo was read as, or what the user corrected it to. Absent until it has been read.

purpose.description: What the product is used for.

usedFor.description: How long the product has been used.

description.description: What the user noted, if anything.

concerns.description: Cautions for a product of unknown contents, worked out from the answers each time the item is shown. Not an analysis of any label.

rulesVersion.description: Which version of the caution rules wrote `concerns`.

noLabel.description: Only on an `unidentified` item: what the user said about the product, and the cautions that earns.

url.description: A path on this API, or an absolute URL for a stock image. A `user` link works for 5 minutes and needs no Authorization header.

kind.description: An `unnamed` product is an ingredient list the label gave no brand and name for: its `brand` and `name` are empty strings and its `category` is `other` unless the label said otherwise.

coverage.description: How much of the regulatory lists the checks cover. A result with no concerns is not an all-clear unless this says so.

photos.description: One `photos` part per photo, in the order the items should appear.

photo.description: A JPEG or WebP photo, at most 2,000,000 bytes and 1600 pixels on the longest side.
A JPEG or WebP photo, at most 2,000,000 bytes and 1600 pixels on the longest side.

text.description: A product name the user typed, 2 to 120 characters once trimmed, with no link, markup or hidden character.

purpose.description: What the product is used for.

usedFor.description: How long the product has been used.

description.description: Anything else the user wants to note, at most 200 characters once trimmed, with no link, markup or hidden character. Blank is the same as left out.

get.summary: Follow a product scan live, as server-sent events
get.description: A `text/event-stream`, not the usual envelope (errors before the stream starts still are). Frames: `snapshot` first, whose data is the scan exactly as `GET /api/v1/scans/products/{scanId}` returns it; then one `item` per change, whose data is the item as that response shows it; then `done` (data `{}`) once every item is `ready`, `rejected`, `failed` or `unidentified`, after which the server closes the stream. A scan that is already finished gets `snapshot` and `done` at once. A `: ping` comment arrives every 20 seconds while nothing else does. The server closes a stream 10 minutes after it opened; reconnect to carry on, the new `snapshot` is the current state. Send the bearer token as for every other route, which a browser `EventSource` cannot: use `fetch` and read the body. Another user's scan is 404, the same as one that does not exist.

post.summary: Name the product of an item whose photo could not be read
post.description: For an item in `needs-retake` or `needs-identification`. Send exactly one of `productId` (picked from `GET /api/v1/products/search`; no model is called) or `text` (a name the user typed, which is split into brand, name and variant by a model: 400 `NOT_A_PRODUCT_NAME` when it is not a product's name, 503 `AI_UNAVAILABLE` when the model is unavailable, 503 `CATALOG_BUSY` when the daily AI budget is spent). The item goes on to matching, researching, analysing or ready. It sends no photo, so no photo quota or retake is used.

post.summary: Say a product has no label to read
post.description: For an item in `needs-identification` (its 3rd front photo could not be read), and no other state: 409 `ITEM_NOT_AWAITING_NO_LABEL`. Send where the product came from, what it is used for and for how long (fixed words), and optionally a short `description` (400 `INVALID_PRODUCT_TEXT` when it is over 200 characters or carries a link, markup or hidden character). The item ends as `unidentified`, which is final, with `noLabel` holding the answers and the cautions for a product of unknown contents. It sends no photo and calls no model, so no photo quota or retake is used.
